## The waterfall and sandstone cliffs

Véu de Noiva, or "Bridal Veil," is located in Chapada dos Guimarães National Park in Mato Grosso. An observation point at the falls offers views of the cascading water and surrounding landscape.

On the eight-day itinerary, the walk to the waterfall concludes an exploration of the park's trails, vegetation, and sandstone cliffs. After this nature-focused excursion, travelers have lunch at a local restaurant and return to their lodge.

The visit involves walking and viewing the waterfall; swimming there is not included in the itinerary. This stop is in a Brazilian national park and should not be confused with waterfalls of the same name in other countries.

Viento Fresco comprises a group of waterfalls near Tilarán. Water cascades among green hillsides and forests, and walking trails let visitors admire the individual falls. This is a nature stop in the mountains of Costa Rica, between the Arenal and Monteverde regions.

The combination of water and lush vegetation, views of the slopes, and small stretches of river beside the cascades make the area rewarding to explore. A walk here offers time in the forest during the journey between larger tourist destinations. The waterfalls add another natural setting to the area's volcanic landscapes and cloud forest.
